title: A Maya painter depicts the rain god on a vessel
summary: A Maya drinking vessel attributed to the Metropolitan Painter depicts the rain god Chahk and other supernatural figures in a finely drawn mythological scene.

claims.text: A Maya drinking vessel attributed to the Metropolitan Painter depicts the rain god Chahk and other supernatural figures in a finely drawn mythological scene.
The collection catalogue gives 600–800 CE for this vessel, not for the entire Maya painted-ceramic tradition.
Such codex-style ceramics combine imagery with hieroglyphic writing. Their proposed production around Calakmul and northern Petén remains an attribution rather than a known workshop address.

review.corroboration: The Met’s thematic essay was compared with its object catalogue. This checks scope and date within one institution, not through independent source families.
